Festive Baked Goat Cheese with Herbs and Honey

Served at: Feast of the Ass

Serves 4-6 as an appetizerPrep 10 minCook 15-20 min

The Feast of the Ass, a unique medieval festival often celebrated around the New Year, was a time of joyous revelry and communal gathering. While specific culinary traditions for this historical celebration are scarce, simple yet elegant dishes that could be shared amongst friends and family would have been cherished. This warm, savory, and sweet baked goat cheese offers a delightful appetizer perfect for a festive table, embodying a spirit of rustic elegance.

Ingredients

  • 8 ounces (225 g) fresh goat cheese log (chevre)
  • 1 tablespoon (15 mL) olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon (5 mL) fresh rosemary, finely chopped
  • 1 teaspoon (5 mL) fresh thyme, finely chopped
  • 2 tablespoons (30 mL) honey
  • 1/4 cup (30 g) chopped walnuts or pecans (optional)
  • Crusty bread, baguette slices, or crackers for serving

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. Place the goat cheese log in a small, oven-safe baking dish or ramekin that is just slightly larger than the cheese.
  3. Drizzle the olive oil evenly over the goat cheese.
  4. Sprinkle the chopped fresh rosemary and thyme over the cheese.
  5. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, or until the goat cheese is warmed through and slightly softened and gooey in the center.
  6. Carefully remove the baking dish from the oven.
  7. Drizzle the honey generously over the warm goat cheese.
  8. If using, sprinkle the chopped walnuts or pecans over the top.
  9. Serve immediately directly from the baking dish with slices of crusty bread, baguette, or your favorite crackers for dipping.

Tips

  • Experiment with other fresh herbs like oregano or marjoram for a different flavor profile.
  • For a touch of heat, add a pinch of red pepper flakes along with the herbs before baking.
  • Serve alongside fig jam or apricot preserves for an extra layer of sweetness and fruitiness.
